ideas: Everyday habits your family has around waste
Who started these habits and why
Something you'd like your family to do next

phrases.meaning: plastic used once, then thrown away
bags you can use many times
be thrown away without being used
give old things to younger people
behave in a way others copy

model: I'd like to talk about how my family reduces waste at home, and honestly, most of it comes from my mum. She grew up when money was tight, so she hates it when anything goes to waste. For example, she always plans meals carefully, and we eat the leftovers the next day for lunch instead of throwing them away. She also takes reusable shopping bags to the market, and she refuses plastic bags so often that the sellers now know her and don't even offer them. A couple of years ago, I read an article about single-use plastic in the ocean, and I showed it to my family. After that, we started to sort the rubbish into plastic, paper and food waste, and my younger brother, who's quite competitive, turned it into a kind of game. Clothes are another thing. In our family, we hand down clothes to cousins, so hardly anything ends up in the bin. I think my mum really sets a good example, and I've copied a lot of her habits in my own flat. The next step I'd like us to take is to make compost from our vegetable scraps. My parents have a small garden, so if we made compost, we wouldn't need to buy fertiliser any more. If I can find a simple compost bin this month, I'll give it to them as a present. I'm quite proud of what we do, even though it's nothing dramatic.
